Fruits basket season 3 Tohru and Kureno character rant; SPOILER WARNING

~!Alright people are saying that Fruits basket is geniusly written because it shows the paralles of Tohru and Akito as in a sense that both of them were outcasts (The onigiri in the fruits basket and the god of the zodiacs) thus it is completely understandable that these two share a deep understanding which is why Tohru showed such kindness towards Akito despite injuring her but it just doesn't justify how Tohru could completely ignore and forgive every bad thing that Akito did. If a criminal in the real world stabbed someone and then stated "I felt lonely and I was hurt that's why I did it" everyone would still hate that person because it simply doesn't justify shit. Tohru can't relate to Akito just because they are both outcasts because Tohru cannot possibly justify for example why Akito stabbed Kureno when even Akito herself doesn't even really understand why she did it. Talking about Kureno. Kureno's character in the first place is unrealisitc beyond comprehension. If my fucking mom stabbed me be sure I ain't gonna get near her anymore no matter how much I love her. Kureno's character lacks reason, why is he staying loyal to Akito no matter what she does? Because he pities her? Alright and? Wait that's it? Are you kidding me? Fruits basket was always good at writing characters, their feelings, motives and facettes but unfortunately it somehow failed with Kureno. I cannot understand his reason which makes it hard for me to feel bad for him even after he got stabbed because his character is so unrealistic to the point that I remember that he is just a written character, a flawed character on top of it. I really wanna love this season but so far it does nothing but make me cringe at the ridiculousness which is sad because Fruits basket became my favourite shoujo anime with season 2.!~

Since both have it's pros and cons, here, I'd say just start with whichever one you like more:

Zero focuses a lot more on creating a detailed battle royale. Characters get roughly equal screentime, so you get to choose who you root for if you start with Zero, and you get to see their ideals and how those ideals clash with each other. On the other hand it's (obviously) lacking a 'main cast' so you'll have less attachment to wach character and doesn't do much more than the battle royale itself, no big plot twists or anything. And as mentioned above it does no explanation which especially hurts it's ending, which is btw kinda anticlimactic because it has to be that way to work with how SN starts. Zero's battles aren't as stunning or exciting as UBW and HF but still pretty damn good.

SN focuses a lot more on Shirou, his development (and he develops differently in each route which is really interesting), and the characters around him, especially the 3 main girls. You can get more attached to these characters especially since the total runtime of all 3 routes is almost triple that of Zero. But ofc in turn some other characters get focused on less, something that might bother people staring with Zero. There also isn't that focus on showing each character's philosophy. You also have to piece information together from 3 routes to get the full picture (altho each route makes perfect sense on their own too, but watching only one isn't as good as all 3 together), which I think is incredibly cool and allows to do more than a regular straightforward anime, but it might be weird to some. UBW also has my favourite plot twist of all time, and generally SN is more surpsing, does more than just a battle royale, essentially only using it to do something bigger, and will keep you on the edge of your seat more. Violet Evergarden: The movie __SPOILER WARNING__

I just finished Violet Evergarden: The movie. Oh god it's really over. That was the conclusion. It's so bittersweet I am honestly so moved. Currently I am feeling this weird mixture of satisfaction and disappointment since I thought "Great the movie is 2 hours long that's why we will get to see many scenes with Violet and Gilbert" but we really only got that one scene and we didn't even get to hear her telling him back "I love you too" I swear I was on edge in my seat while waiting for her to respond to him BUT NOTHING. AFTERWARDS WAS NOTHING UGH.

Alright to the good things: I loved this movie. I always know that Violet Evergarden movies won't disappoint me and this one just punched me in the face with its awesomeness. That Gilbert was alive was already obvious to me a long time ago so I really looked forward to this movie and their reunion. Tbh at the beginning I was like "Oh god they are adding extra stories to it please not just go straight to Violet and Gilbert" but in the end I still enjoyed it a lot. What annoyed me at first actually brought me to tears when the "Sidestory" concluded. Violet Evergarden is a beautiful story and one of the best slowburn tearjerkers I've ever seen. It plays so well with its subtle emotional elements which really hits hard in the end. Of course this movie had a lot of cliches and some plot points were painfully obvious but all in all they utilized these cliches so well that it wasn't even boring. Maybe I am getting too swayed by the high production quality and because Violet Evergarden was the only anime that made me cry with such a calming and healing plot but this movie is just another KyoAni masterpiece. I really wished they would have let us at least see granny Violet with Gilbert (I really wanna know if they got kids and how their lifes turned out) I also hoped that Violet might have told the girl a bit about her story but I think I can be satisfied with this conclusion.

It was a beautiful journey. Goodbye, Violet Evergarden.

This show is my favourite because I find a lot of joy in those "Aha!" moments where you build up something for a whole season and only realise a lot later what the characters meant 20 episodes ago.
